explanation: The second king of Israel, who succeeded King Saul and united the twelve tribes.
A city in the Middle East, also known as Zion, which David made the capital of his kingdom.
A fortified structure or building used for defense and protection.
The king of Tyre, who helped David build his palace by sending materials and craftsmen.
A people who lived in Canaan and were enemies of the Israelites. David defeated them several times.
A name for a fortress in Jerusalem, meaning "shame of Baal." David captured it from the Jebusites.
The inhabitants of Jerusalem before David conquered the city. They belonged to one of the Canaanite tribes.
The Almighty Creator who, according to Genesis, created heaven, earth, and all life.
A holy relic that contained the stone tablets with the Ten Commandments and symbolized God's presence among the Israelites.
